key_insight: A calibrated Extreme Gradient Boosting model accurately predicted cervical cancer screening use in Ethiopian women and highlighted major social and access-related drivers of screening.
clinical_relevance: This could help public health teams identify women less likely to be screened and target outreach, triage, and community engagement more efficiently.
method: Nationally representative secondary analysis of the 2024/25 Ethiopian Demographic and Health Survey (women aged 15–49).
Compared six supervised machine-learning models, with class imbalance addressed using SMOTE.
Used SHAP for explainability plus discrimination, calibration, and decision-curve evaluation.
evidence_signal: Extreme Gradient Boosting performed best (AUROC 0.896, AUPRC 0.781), and isotonic calibration improved prediction with a Brier score of 0.038.
watch_item: Because screening prevalence was very low and the study used holdout validation rather than external validation, real-world performance and generalizability should be confirmed before deployment.
paper_title: Predicting Cervical Cancer Screening Utilization Among Women of Reproductive Age in Ethiopia Using Supervised Machine Learning: A Nationally Representative 2024/25 EDHS Study
